messages:
jon: Heads-up — planning a small cross-svc canary tonight during the 23:00 UTC change window. Question: do we want to pin the router+console to the new runtime API version for the entire 30m canary, or only pin during the first 10m spike?

maya: I lean toward pinning for the full 30m. Runtime changes can cause subtle header/kv mismatches and we want a stable surface for debugging.

lee: Router depends on the new header contract for session affinity. If we unpin early the rollout may start routing to mixed variants and we'll lose signal. +1 for full 30m pin.

oliver: Console team prefers unpinned after warmup so dashboards show traffic degradation across variants. But we can do a strict pinned-first-phase then unpin if metrics look good.

jon: So proposal: Phase A (0-10m) pinned: api v2.1, runtime v2.1, router v2.1, console pinned UI+agent. Phase B (10-30m) router+api stay pinned, console unpinned. Runtime keep pinned unless latency/regressions.

samantha: Sounds reasonable. Need explicit rollback criteria. I'd say: any p95 increase >200ms vs baseline OR error-rate >0.5% absolute for 5m -> immediate rollback. Also volume drop >20%/5m flagged for manual.

maya: Agree. Also add KV hit-rate drop >5% sustained 3m as a soft-alert; might indicate cache eviction behavior from kernel changes.

engops-bot: Preflight check: all services report compatible model schema. Runtime: OK. API: OK. Router: OK. Console: UI agent version mismatches WARN.

oliver: I'll patch the console agent to align; will push a tiny fix to match runtime schema in next 20m.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: scheduled canary start at 2026-03-23T23:00Z. Targets: runtime:v2.1, api:v2.1, router:v2.1, console: canary agent v2.1 (pinned-phase).

jon: Quick note on pin semantics — use pin-mode=hard for router and runtime (no serving of older variants), console uses pin-mode=soft (UI can show mixed). Command: 

```
# pin router/runtime hard for wave-7990
rd-deploy pin --service router --variant v2.1 --mode hard --expires 00:30:00
rd-deploy pin --service runtime --variant v2.1 --mode hard --expires 00:30:00
rd-deploy pin --service console --variant v2.1 --mode soft --expires 00:10:00
```

lee: Confirmed those CLI flags exist. Will monitor routing heatmaps and affinity buckets.

samantha: Who's oncall for quick rollback and DB access if we need to revert migrations?

maya: I'm primary for runtime, lee for router, oliver for console. Sam backup.

jon: OK final checklist: 
- oliver pushes console agent fix (in-flight)
- engops: run smoke against staging prod-slice 10m before window
- deploy-bot: start canary, then run telemetry job at 0/5/10/20/30m
- rollback triggers as stated above

oliver: console fix pushed -> PR merged, image building now. Will post image digest in thread when ready.

engops-bot: Smoke-run scheduled 22:50Z -> results: OK (latency within baseline, no errors).

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary started. wave id: 7990. Pin states applied.

jon: Starting telemetry checks now. 0m: all green. p95 within +12ms, error-rate 0.02%.

lee: Router heatmap shows stickiness consistent; no cross-variant bleed.

maya: Runtime metrics: CPU up ~6%, kv hit stable. No reg signs.

jon: At 10m: unpin console (soft->unpin) per plan unless objections.

oliver: No objections, unpinning console now.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: console unpinned.

jon: 15m check: p95 +18ms, error-rate 0.03%, KV hit -1%. Still within thresholds.

lee: continuing to monitor affinity buckets.

samatha_typo: (typo) all good from infra side.

samantha: Noted — typo accepted :grin:. All good from my side. If anything spikes I'll flag immediate rollback.

jon: All right — finishing up 30m post-canary summary and will update release notes. If nothing hits rollback thresholds we'll proceed to gradual full rollout at 02:00 UTC with a 3-hour ramp.

oliver: Posting console image digest: sha256:abcdef1234567890.

deploy-bot: deploy-bot: canary wave 7990 completed at 23:30Z. No auto-rollbacks triggered.

jon: Thank you everyone. I'll draft release notes and pin the rollout plan in the release doc. If anyone wants follow-up retrospective, let's sync tomorrow 10:00 UTC.
